```console
sections/method.tex:12:\paragraph{Fragility $k^\*$.}
sections/method.tex:13:$k^\*(a\succ b)$ is the smallest number of alterations after which the exact refit has $\theta_a-\theta_b\le 0$. It is found by search and is a \emph{verified upper bound}: the search proposes alterations by first-order influence (the effect of one alteration on the gap, $H^{-1}$-propagated as in influence functions~\cite{koh2017}), fills the budget with the most effective ones, refits exactly, and re-linearises at the refit (iterated re-linearisation); a Frank--Wolfe pass on the continuous relaxation is a second proposer. The number of alterations is found by bisection on the budget. Let $g_{\max}$ be the largest first-order effect of a single alteration on the gap; $k_{\mathrm{lin}}$ is the first-order estimate (the smallest $k$ whose $k$ largest effects sum to the gap) without refit.
sections/method.tex:16:For a fixed conclusion, the statistical separation is $z\propto\Delta\sqrt N$ and the largest influence decreases with $N$, so the raw share $k^\*/N$ is not comparable between datasets of different size; theory for top-$K$ ranking gives the same $1/\sqrt N$ rate for the estimation error~\cite{chen2019}. We therefore express fragility in standard-error units, $F=k^\*g_{\max}/\mathrm{SE}$, and the dimensionless ratio $Q=F/z=k^\*g_{\max}/\Delta$. $Q$ equals~1 in the first-order regime if all single-alteration effects were equal to $g_{\max}$; exact refit and the shape of the influence distribution move it, depending on the family and the comparison graph. $Q$ is therefore read only against its own reference (below).
```

```console
# Reproduction (analysis part; draft, completed when the runs are final)

All code is in `code/` (`code/src` library, `code/scripts` entry points); results tables in `results/`. Raw data are **not** in the repository.

## Environment
Python 3.11, numpy, scipy, pandas, pyarrow (versions recorded by `pip freeze` in `code/ENVIRONMENT.txt` when finalised). CPU only, no GPU, no network after the data download.

## Data (download into `$BT_DATA`, default `/hutian/data`)
| directory | source (pinned commit) | file | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `arena55k/train.csv` | HF `lmarena-ai/arena-human-preference-55k` @ `18c298340948c0e7f7727399fd459cca6ce0ca6f` | train.csv | `0692154aaf20fc6649090c3f49b6b5dd1e693a765ecb5f0856ae0da5946f5be2` |
| `mtbench/human.parquet` | HF `lmsys/mt_bench_human_judgments` @ `f7d2896d2cc5d80f8b55c2bbc722613555233c25` | `data/human-00000-of-00001-25f4910818759289.parquet` | `4877bc46a40929f4082c3c79593700fb897b1d6c7f4c473032694a01322f5769` |
| `mtbench/gpt4_pair.parquet` | same | `data/gpt4_pair-00000-of-00001-c0b431264a82ddc0.parquet` | `57068327ffb5f8fddb15fedbbfe40b26fe862da2326331e5cf64a42320a00e71` |
| `potsawee/train.single-turn.json`, `potsawee/prob-avg/<judge>.jsonl` | HF `potsawee/chatbot-arena-llm-judges` @ `638a7e3be3078e55d2eb0b789d34749747822c49` (`llm-judges-prob-avg/`) | | `6ed8793f61931637b65c1f348e8cb3a050996eef2a8c5c37c0b42fcfe465c8f3` (json) |
| `nba/nbaallelo.csv` | GitHub `fivethirtyeight/data` @ `4c1ff5e3aef1816ae04af63218015066e186c147`, `nba-elo/nbaallelo.csv` | | `d46ed3540ee8d9eca31b3e94cc8c777e0be5156173d814ebf65b8195e8d616bc` |

Download: `curl -fsSL https://huggingface.co/datasets/<repo>/resolve/<commit>/<file>`; raw GitHub URL for NBA. The sha256 of the first four entries equal those in the task's `data.md`.
The judges' license is not declared by the dataset; its README states the data derive from the Kaggle LMSYS competition data (Arena-55k is apache-2.0).

## Commands (4 CPUs)
1. `scripts/run_core_all.sh 500 20` : per data set all-pair k\*, z, Q, bootstrap (B=500 cluster + 500 comparison) and 20 null replicates (Arena-55k ~14 min, 19 Arena units ~1 h on 4 cores); `scripts/run_core_nba.sh` for NBA seasons.
2. `scripts/02_random.py UNIT`, `03_search_validity.py`, `04_synthetic.py`, `04b_synthetic_pflip.py`, `05_scaling.py UNIT` : baselines, search quality, synthetic checks, subsampling.
3. `scripts/06_tables.py` : the CSV tables in `results/`.
Seeds: `--seed 0` everywhere; replicates use `np.random.default_rng([seed, tag, rep])`.

See `PREANALYSIS.md` for the fixed definitions and decision margins.
```
